summary: The 2026-08-29 fixes did land — the port no longer throws the array-budget runtime error (clean at 800 frames @20 fps and 480 frames @2 fps) — but it still draws nothing resembling the subject: the original renders a large gold/white flaming eye with a black vertical slit pupil filling the 16x16 grid (mean brightness 31, 64% of pixels lit, core railed at 255,255,255, texture decorrelating in <0.5 s), while the port emits ~30 near-black dark-red specks (mean brightness 0, 12% lit, peak channel 27-57, blue channel exactly 0 in every frame of every run, total light output ~1.5% of the original's) that barely change over 20 s, at every dial setting, grid size and seed.
observations: CRASH FIXED (regression check): no runtimeError or compileError on either side in any run, including rj-long40 (--seconds 40 --fps 20, 800 rendered frames) and rj-survey240 (--seconds 240 --fps 2, 480 frames). The prior verdict's 'array element budget exceeded at frame 512' failure is gone. This is the only observable improvement.

Untouched baseline (rj-baseline, 6 s @20 fps, 16x16 grid): orig meanBrightness avg 31.4 (min 26, max 38), meanR 56.2 / meanG 32.3 / meanB 5.6, motion avg 6.1, motionLit 9.4, zeroMotionFrames 1, brightnessTrend steady. Port meanBrightness avg 0.0 (min 0, max 0), meanR 1 / meanG 0 / meanB 0, motion avg 0 on all 120 frames, motionLit avg 0.0 (max 0.1), zeroMotionFrames 120/120. The port is now DIMMER than at the prior judging (meanBrightness 0 vs the previously recorded 1).

Original structure (--dump at t=3.4 s on the default 16x16 rig, rj-dump1): a filled horizontally-elongated ellipse spanning rows 2-13 and columns 1-14 — i.e. essentially the whole rig — 165/256 pixels lit, values climbing from a 1-9 rim through 40-150 mid-tones to pixels at exactly 255,255,255, with a dark hole (values 0-1) at rows 7-9, columns 7-8: the pupil. Colour ramps dark-red -> orange -> yellow -> white.

Port structure at the identical moment: 32/256 pixels lit, brightest pixel 35,1,0. The lit pixels are ~8 isolated 1-3 px specks loosely clustered around rows 4-11, columns 2-12 — no elliptical body, no rim, no pupil, no continuous field. Nothing in the image reads as an eye at any moment sampled.

Colour envelope over 5376 dumped pixels spanning five separate runs and dial settings: orig litFrac 64.5%, peak pixel [255,255,255], maxG 255, maxB 255. Port litFrac 12.1%, peak pixel [57,8,0], maxG 8, maxB **0** — the port's blue channel never leaves zero in a single pixel of a single frame anywhere, and green never exceeds 8. The port is emitting only the darkest-red foot of a fire ramp.

Total light output (sum of per-pixel max-channel over the frame, rj-lag dumps at t=5,5.05,5.5,7,15,25 s): orig 13,328-15,073 and stable; port 238, 237, 225, 175, 77, 127 — 1.5% to 0.5% of the original, and drifting downward over the window. Centroids: orig pinned at (7.6, 7.5) +/-0.2 px (the eye is stationary and centred); port wanders (8.3,6.5) -> (9.0,6.5) -> (7.8,7.4) -> (9.2,7.9).

Motion character (rj-lag, --fps 20, meanAbsDiff of frame at t=5 against later frames): orig 6.15 at 0.05 s lag, saturating at ~16-18 by 0.5 s — the iris texture boils and fully decorrelates within half a second. Port 0.01 at 0.05 s, 0.07 at 0.5 s, 0.21 at 2 s, 0.38 at 10 s, 0.39 at 20 s — it reaches its (tiny) plateau only after ~10 s. Even after normalizing for the ~8.5x peak-brightness gap, the port's per-frame texture change is ~70x too slow; unnormalized it is ~600x.

Survey (rj-survey, 60 s @5 fps) and extended survey (rj-survey240, 240 s @2 fps): the original's rhythm image is a uniformly bright gold column with continuous fine flicker top to bottom — no regimes, no mode rotation, no long-period cycle (meanBrightness avg 31.4, min 26, max 38 over the whole 240 s; brightnessTrend steady). The port's rhythm image is solid black with a few barely-visible dark-red wisps (meanBrightness avg 0.1, max 1). There is no mode structure on either side, so short windows are representative.

Resolution independence (rj-grid48, --grid 48x48): the original draws THE SAME eye, just finer — an elliptical body of radiating white-hot flame filaments around a clean black vertical slit pupil, occupying the same fraction of the rig as at 16x16 (mean 33.8 vs 31.4). It is resolution-independent, drawing into a logical canvas. The port at 48x48 still shows only 4-6 dim red blobs near the centre-left, mean brightness 0.0 — no eye, no rim, no pupil, and the blobs do not resolve into any finer structure.
Seed 1234 (rj-seed1234) reproduces both sides unchanged (orig mean 31.3, port mean 0.0) — this is not a seed fluke.

CONTROL NAME MISMATCH persists: the original exposes sliderAngularDensity, sliderRadialDensity, sliderDialation (label 'Dialation' — the author's spelling), sliderSlitness. The port exposes sliderAngularDensity, sliderRadialDensity, sliderDilation (label 'Dilation'), sliderSlitness. The port silently corrected the third control's spelling, so the original's saved value or any external set of 'sliderDialation' does not bind on the port at all.

Dial triage (rj-probe, 4 s @20 fps): all four ORIGINAL dials responsive, maxDeltaLit 11.2-28.7 (AngularDensity 28.68, RadialDensity 28.69, Slitness 19.42, Dialation 11.18). All four PORT dials read NOT responsive: AngularDensity maxDeltaLit 2.66, RadialDensity 2.27, Dilation 0.10, Slitness 0.05. Manually confirmed over 40 s @10 fps windows and 30 s dump comparisons (see dials).

Explicitly-dialed comparisons at all-0, all-0.5 and all-1 (rj-dial-*, 12 s @10 fps, same values both sides using each side's own spelling for the third slider): orig meanBrightness 23.3 / 28.7 / 27.7; port 0.6 / 0.0 / 0.0 with zeroMotionFrames 120/120 in all three. The divergence is not an untouched-defaults artefact — the port is dead at every dialed setting too.

dials.name: sliderAngularDensity
dials.origEffect: Angular fineness of the flame texture in the iris. At 0 the eye is broader and smoother with fewer, larger dark voids (40 s @10 fps: meanBrightness 22.2, meanR 43.9/G 20.7/B 1.9, motionLit 12.4); at 1 the interior breaks into many finer angularly-spaced filaments and the whole body brightens (meanBrightness 28.9, R 53.1/G 29.2/B 4.3, motionLit 14.9). Probe maxDeltaLit 28.68 — the strongest dial. Dump comparison 0 vs 1 over three widely-spaced times: meanAbsDiff 17.26, maxDiff 255.
dials.portEffect: The strongest of the port's four dials, and still visually nothing. Probe maxDeltaLit 2.66; 40 s @10 fps sweep gives meanBrightness 0.1 at 0 and 0.0 at 1, motionLit 0.1 for both, zeroMotionFrames 400/400 for both. Dump 0 vs 1: meanAbsDiff 0.41 (vs 17.26 on the original), lit pixels 119 -> 85 of 768, peak channel 30 -> 57. Both settings render the same near-black dark-red speck field.

dials.name: sliderRadialDensity
dials.origEffect: Radial counterpart — how finely the iris is striated from pupil to rim. Aggregate brightness barely moves (40 s @10 fps: meanBrightness 28.8 at both 0 and 1, motionLit 14.8/14.9) because it redistributes rather than adds light, but the image changes substantially: probe maxDeltaLit 28.69 and a dump comparison of 0 vs 1 gives meanAbsDiff 13.49 with maxDiff 255. At 0 the flame filaments are broad radial spokes; at 1 they are fine concentric striations reaching further into the rim.
dials.portEffect: Effectively inert. Probe maxDeltaLit 2.27; 40 s sweep meanBrightness 0.0 at both, motionLit 0.1 both, zeroMotionFrames 400/400. Dump 0 vs 1 meanAbsDiff 0.34, lit 102 -> 92 of 768, peak 33 -> 39. No structural change of any kind.

dials.name: sliderDialation (port spells it sliderDilation)
dials.origEffect: Pupil aperture. At 0 the pupil is nearly closed and the eye is a near-solid bright body (40 s @10 fps: meanBrightness 34.5, meanR 60.8/G 36.4/B 6.3, motionLit 16.9); at 1 a wide dark vertical pupil opens through the centre and cuts the body in two, dropping brightness by 40% (meanBrightness 20.5, R 39.9/G 19.5/B 2.2, motionLit 12.4) and lit pixels from 505 to 427 per three dumped frames. Probe maxDeltaLit 11.18; dump 0 vs 1 meanAbsDiff 13.38, maxDiff 255.
dials.portEffect: Inert. Probe maxDeltaLit 0.10; 40 s @10 fps sweep at 0 vs 1 gives identical meanBrightness 0.0, meanR 0.6, motionLit 0.1, zeroMotionFrames 400/400 for both. Dump 0 vs 1 over three times 15 s apart: meanAbsDiff 0.02, lit 93 -> 87 of 768, peak channel 27 at both. Nothing resembling a pupil exists to open. NOTE the control-surface bug: addressing this dial by the original's name (sliderDialation) does not bind on the port at all.

dials.name: sliderSlitness
dials.origEffect: Pupil/centre shape and overall agitation. At 0 the dark centre is a ragged multi-armed starburst and the whole eye is markedly dimmer and redder (40 s @10 fps: meanBrightness 15.7, meanR 35.0/G 12.0/B 0.0, motionLit 9.8); at 1 it collapses to a single clean narrow vertical slit and the body is brighter and reaches white (meanBrightness 31.5, R 56.7/G 32.6/B 5.2, motionLit 15.9). This is the biggest brightness swing of any dial: 2x. Probe maxDeltaLit 19.42; dump 0 vs 1 meanAbsDiff 15.34, maxDiff 255, peak channel 227 -> 255.
dials.portEffect: Inert. Probe maxDeltaLit 0.05 (the weakest of all eight side/dial combinations); 40 s sweep meanBrightness 0.0 at both, meanR 0.5 vs 0.6, motionLit 0.1 both. Dump 0 vs 1 meanAbsDiff 0.02, lit 86 -> 93, peak 27 at both settings.

feedback: The two 2026-08-29 fixes did what they claimed narrowly — no runtime error at 800 frames @20 fps or 480 frames @2 fps — but neither touched the rendering failure. Treat the crash as closed and start over on the image.

The port never draws the subject. The original's entire image is ONE large eye: a horizontally-elongated ellipse centred on the rig, ~14 px wide by ~12 px tall on 16x16, lighting 64% of all pixels as a CONTINUOUS FIELD (not specks), graded from a 1-9 value rim through orange/yellow mid-tones to a white-hot 255,255,255 core, with a dark vertical pupil (values 0-1) occupying about 2x3 px at the centre. The port lights 12% of pixels as ~8 disconnected 1-3 px specks with no body, no rim and no pupil. Rebuild the shape and the field continuity first; every other finding below is downstream of that.

Brightness is off by roughly two orders of magnitude, and the gap has WIDENED since the last judging: total per-frame light output (sum of max-channel over all pixels) is 13,300-15,100 on the original versus 77-238 on the port — 0.5-1.8%. Peak channel is 255 on the original and 27-57 on the port across every run, dial setting, grid size and seed. Some single scalar in the value path (a radius/falloff term, a noise normalization, an intensity multiplier) is collapsing the result to near zero; find it before chasing anything structural, because at this magnitude nothing else can be assessed.

The port's blue channel is EXACTLY ZERO in every pixel of every frame across five separate dump runs (maxB 0), and green never exceeds 8. The original's palette runs dark-red -> orange -> yellow -> pure white, averaging R 56 / G 32 / B 5.6 with maxG and maxB both hitting 255. This is consistent with the same root cause as the brightness collapse — a fire-style palette indexed by a value that never leaves its darkest-red foot — so a correct value scale may fix both at once. Verify by checking that the port can reach 255,255,255 anywhere before assuming the palette itself is wrong.

The port's texture is also far too slow, independent of brightness. At 20 fps the original's frame-to-frame meanAbsDiff is 6.15 and it fully decorrelates within 0.5 s (the iris visibly boils); the port's is 0.01 at 0.05 s and only reaches its plateau of 0.39 after ~10 s. Normalized for the 8.5x peak gap that is still ~70x too slow. Whatever advances the noise field per frame is running at a small fraction of the original's rate.

The eye must be STATIONARY. The original's brightness centroid sits at (7.6, 7.5) +/-0.2 px over a 20 s window; the port's wanders between (7.8, 6.5) and (9.2, 7.9). The original animates only its interior texture and pupil, never its body position.

All four dials are dead on the port and all four are strong on the original — fix the render, then verify each against these targets: AngularDensity 0->1 should visibly break the iris into finer angular filaments and raise mean brightness 22 -> 29; RadialDensity 0->1 should change broad radial spokes into fine concentric striation at roughly constant mean brightness (28.8 both ends) but a large per-pixel change (meanAbsDiff 13.5); Dialation 0->1 should open a wide dark vertical pupil, dropping mean brightness 34.5 -> 20.5; Slitness 0->1 should morph a ragged multi-armed dark starburst into one clean narrow slit while brightness doubles 15.7 -> 31.5. Port probe maxDeltaLit is currently 0.05-2.66 against the original's 11.2-28.7.

Restore the control NAME: the original's third slider is sliderDialation (label 'Dialation' — the author's misspelling). The port renamed it sliderDilation. Even once rendering works, saved values and any external control call using the original's name will silently miss the port's dial.

Preserve resolution independence. The original draws the same eye occupying the same fraction of the rig at 16x16 and at 48x48, gaining only finer flame detail (mean brightness 31.4 vs 33.8). Draw into a normalized logical canvas; do not rasterize features at native pixel resolution.
